result.text:
I added all three features to the crawler that was already in the image, and all 44 tests pass (the 16 original ones plus 28 new ones).

## Design
The old crawler had four `CrawlerFacing` classes and a string of `ifTrue:` checks for each command. I kept the facings and replaced the `ifTrue:` chain with objects that take turns handling each case.

- **Commands:** there is one class per command character (`CrawlerAdvanceCommand`, `CrawlerRetreatCommand`, the two turn commands, `CrawlerStartGuardedRunCommand` and `CrawlerEndGuardedRunCommand`). `CrawlerCommand for:ifNone:` finds the right one.
- **Repetition:** after each command the crawler remembers `command asRepeatableCommand`. Advance, retreat and the two turns return themselves. Anything else returns `CrawlerNonRepeatableCommand`, which raises "invalid command" if a digit follows. After a digit the remembered command is reset, so `a00` is invalid. It is also reset at the start of each new command string.
- **Sonar:** the crawler takes a sonar that answers `groundTypeAt:`. The answer is one of three ground classes:
  - `SeabedFirmSand` moves the crawler normally.
  - `SeabedBoulder` raises an error, both when moving onto it and when turning on it.
  - `SeabedSilt` makes the crawler slide `direction * (random nextInteger: 10)` cells. When retreating, it slides backwards.

  Facings now just give a direction (such as `0@1`), which replaced the old `moveUp`/`moveDown` methods.
- **Guarded runs:** the crawler is always in one of two modes, `CrawlerFreeRun` or `CrawlerGuardedRun`.
  - In a guarded run, every move or turn saves a step that undoes it, and silt raises an error instead of sliding.
  - An error happens if you open a run inside another, close one that isn't open, or leave one unclosed at the end of the string.
  - `process:` catches any `Error`, has the current mode undo its steps in reverse order, returns to free mode, and then sends `pass` to raise the error again.

## Tests and constructor
- The test class is now in `SurveyCrawler-Tests`. So are two test stand-ins: `SonarSimulator` (lets a test place boulders and silt; everything else is firm sand) and `FixedRandom` (returns a fixed slide and records the limit it was asked for, so a test can check it is 10).
- **Constructor change:** a crawler is now created with `at:facing:sonar:`, or with `at:facing:sonar:random:` to supply the random generator. I removed the old `at:facing:` and updated the old tests to match.

## Choices the spec didn't cover
- **Undoing doesn't use the sonar.** The crawler goes straight back over positions it has already been on. Otherwise, if a guarded run started on silt, going back would make it slide and it could never return to its starting position (test44 covers this).
- **Silt in a guarded run doesn't slide at all.** The error is raised before moving, so nothing random needs to be undone.
- **Errors outside a guarded run undo nothing.** Moves made before the error are kept, as before. If a guarded run fails, only that run's moves are undone, not earlier finished runs.
- **Sliding doesn't check the cells it passes over.** A slide can end on or cross a boulder, because the spec only asks the sonar about the cell the command lands on.
- **Other invalid cases:** a digit at the start of a string, or right after `(` or `)`, is an invalid command.
